scraped.title: Gender Directive for Basic Education
scraped.subtitle: Development of a Gender Directive for Basic Education for the Ministry of Education and Culture in Mozambique
scraped.description: Recent studies on gender equality in Mozambique put in the spotlight feminisation of poverty, analysis of dropouts in primary education by gender, and female unfavourable completion rates. Although in the last decade Mozambique has advanced in increasing enrolment and…
body: Recent studies on gender equality in Mozambique put in the spotlight feminisation of poverty, analysis of dropouts in primary education by gender, and female unfavourable completion rates. Although in the last decade Mozambique has advanced in increasing enrolment and reducing gender gaps in primary education, the female rate in Mozambique is lower than in both Sub-Saharan Africa and the low-income group of countries, due to poverty, poor school and teaching conditions, and a lack of adequate sanitation. The most frequently named notion associated with gender-related situation in the country is School-Related Gender-Based Violence, mirroring the violence and unrest in communities that are based on prevailing behavioural norms and established social stereotypes.

The GIZ-initiated project ‘Development of a gender guideline for school education for the Ministry of Education and Culture in Mozambique’ is to support the Mozambican Ministry of Education and Culture and the Gender Working Group in developing a practical and results-oriented gender guideline for primary education. The policy draws on best practices from Mozambique and the region and provides concrete guidelines for coordinating, implementing and monitoring measures to promote gender equality and equity in primary education. It also contains specific guidelines on preventing and combating gender-based violence in schools in order to improve girls' learning outcomes.
